analysis: CORRECTION: the market has actually already moved to Packers -3.5, total 39.5 -- an earlier same-day fetch (from a source that hadn't refreshed) had this backwards, showing the line softening toward Tampa Bay after Baker Mayfield's injury, which never happened. In reality the market caught up to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels making his first NFL start almost immediately, tightening the spread edge from what looked like a wide ~4-point gap down to about 2.1 points once corrected.

The total tells the more surprising story: the model (41.0) now sits slightly ABOVE the corrected market (39.5) -- the opposite of the pre-correction read. That's not a total lean in either direction on a gap this small, but it's worth noting Green Bay's own offensive line has been shaky the last two weeks (Jordan Love under heavy, repeated pressure) -- plausibly exactly why the market isn't pricing this total any lower despite Tampa Bay's clear QB downgrade. The spread remains the cleaner side of this game, tempered from a strong lean to a real-but-modest one now that the market has largely caught up.
